blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and October 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 53 in June to 34 in October (−35.8%), and it took 24.6% of the city’s 167 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 108 in June to 99 in October (−8.3%), and it took 58.5% of the city’s 193 sales over the period.

The monthly write-ups singled out Clayton for detached houses in July, August, September, October (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in June (a buyers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July, August, September, October (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Clayton
What trades here

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form

Bare-land strata — the form, no Clayton instance known: A bare-land strata lot is strata tenure ON the lot itself: the buyer takes a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the strata's bylaws, and is entitled to a Form B Information Certificate for the lot — it is not fee-simple ownership with a road association. Tenure is read lot by lot on title.
Lot character: there is no Clayton-wide lot-size table.
ALR vs non-ALR split: Clayton Heights runs to the ALR in the north and west.
A lot near Fraser Highway carries plan upside and plan uncertainty until the designations and station are in place.

blocks.text: Where it sits and what to know here

items.t: Municipal geography: the City plans this area as Clayton Heights — approximately 809 hectares (2,000 acres), extending from Fraser Highway in the south to the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) in the north and west, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east. The City's plan neighbourhoods are East Clayton, West Clayton and the not-yet-initiated North Clayton.
East Clayton is located north of Fraser Highway along the border with the Township of Langley; homes east of that boundary are in the Township, not Surrey Clayton.

Planning frame: the Clayton General Land Use Plan (approved January 25, 1999) set up the Neighbourhood Concept Plan process; East Clayton's NCP was endorsed in 2003 and West Clayton's final NCP was approved in July 2015, planned for over 12,000 residents with a mixed-use centre at 184 Street and Fraser Highway. The City records that those NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — confirm a lot's current OCP designation rather than relying on an NCP label alone.
Civic anchor: Clayton Community Centre, 7155 187A Street, opened October 16, 2021 — a 75,000 sq. ft. facility integrating arts, recreation, library, parks and community amenities.
( (as of November 1, 2026))

Transit plan fact: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain project names Hillcrest-184 Street Station (northwest corner of 184 Street and Fraser Highway) and Clayton Station (future intersection of 190 Street and Fraser Highway); TransLink states a 16-km Expo Line extension with an anticipated in-service date of 2029 — a plan, not current service.

Market context, labelled community context only (SnapStats FVR September 2026; land has no SnapStats category): Clayton detached 34 / 10 / 29%; Clayton "Condos & Townhomes" combined 96 / 20 / 21% — the highest ratios in the Cloverdale sub-area set that month. Cloverdale community medians (the board does not publish sub-area medians): detached $1,212,500; attached $740,000. No detached figure is a land figure.

BC strata block (wherever a bare-land strata lot is the purchase — form only; no Clayton instance verified): Form B within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25¢/page; depreciation reports every 5 years for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022; only 55+ age bylaws valid (SPA ss. 123.1/123.2, May 1, 2023 exemptions). A "45+" listing line is not a valid age bylaw.

ALR block (Clayton's north and west edge parcels): ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; principal residence ≤500 m², a suite within the principal residence only, and one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha).

BC Assessment farm class — full three-tier form: $2,500 (farm operation 0.8–4 ha); $2,500 plus 5% of the actual value of the area over 4 ha (>4 ha); $10,000 (under 0.8 ha); applications by October 31. A flat "$2,500+" statement is an error and is not used here.

Clayton moved faster than the rest of Cloverdale in September 2026. Clayton's detached sales ratio was 29% and attached 21%, ahead of the Cloverdale sub-area (13% / 17%), while Serpentine was 0 / 0 / NA in both splits.

The NCP labels are superseded. East and West Clayton NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — a lot marketed on an old NCP label still needs its current OCP designation confirmed with the City.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: streets and boundaries

items.t: East Clayton, the first urban neighbourhood developed in Clayton Heights, sits north of Fraser Highway along the Langley border.
West Clayton is the second urban neighbourhood, adjacent to East Clayton and the ALR.
Clayton is part of Cloverdale in City planning; its land-use plans sit under Cloverdale land-use plans.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: the housing stock

items.t: Clayton was planned from 1999 as a compact community where amenities and services are within walking distance of homes.
East Clayton covers about 314 hectares (776 acres) across four plan areas, including a transit-oriented area on Fraser Highway.
West Clayton covers about 288 hectares (713 acres) north of Fraser Highway, with a mixed-use centre planned at a future rapid transit station at 184 Street and Fraser Highway.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The East Clayton and West Clayton Neighbourhood Concept Plan (NCP) designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) update; the OCP now guides development.
The ALR borders Clayton on the north and west, so lots on those edges adjoin protected farm land.
A land-use plan for North Clayton has not yet been initiated, per the City.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Clayton plan area was divided using elementary school catchments, with boundaries on major roads so students would not need to cross them walking to school.
Hillcrest-184 Street Station, west of Clayton Station, also serves the Clayton edge at 184 Street and Fraser Highway.
The East Clayton Transit Oriented Area plan guides development that integrates with future rapid transit on Fraser Highway.
72 Avenue widening from 188 Street to 196 Street was anticipated complete in fall 2026, on Clayton's north route.
The future 72 Avenue extension from 152 Street to Highway 15 will cross south of Clayton, with bridges over Bear Creek and the Serpentine River.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: costs and taxes

items.t: Surrey's 2025 flat rate for a single-family home was water $1,139 plus sewer $1,638, total $2,777.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: getting around

items.t: Fraser Highway is Clayton's south edge and its transit corridor, with Clayton and Hillcrest-184 Street stations planned on it.
Highway 15 (176 Street) is the main north-south arterial west of Clayton, linking to Highway 1 and the United States border at Pacific Highway.

blocks.text: Clayton Heights: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check north and west edge lots for ALR adjacency and farm-use activity; the ALR bounds Clayton on those sides.
Do not rely on rescinded East or West Clayton NCP maps for permitted use; the City states the OCP now leads development.

faq.q: Is Clayton in Surrey or Langley?
faq.a: Surrey. Clayton Heights runs from Fraser Highway to the ALR, bordered by the Township of Langley in the east — homes east of that boundary are in the Township, with different bylaws, taxes and school district.

faq.q: How many units can a Clayton lot hold?
faq.a: 3 under 280 m², 4 over 280 m², up to 6 on eligible 281 m²+ lots within 400 m of a frequent bus stop — subject to zone, servicing and, on ALR parcels, the ALC caps instead.

faq.q: Can I add a coach house?
faq.a: In zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes, yes — 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR), lane access required for a coach house on smaller R3–R6 lots, one extra parking space.

faq.q: The listing says "RF-12" — is that the lot's zone?
faq.a: Not currently: RF-12 / RF-12C became R4 and RF-SD became R6 on July 8, 2024. Check the lot's current zone in Bylaw 12000 before quoting potential.

faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex in Clayton?
faq.a: Yes, where the side is legally separate — Surrey's R6 semi-detached form is exactly that (paired fee-simple lots at a zero-lot-line common side), and a strata duplex half is a strata lot. A single-lot duplex still sells whole. Check the title first.

faq.q: Who maintains the shared wall on an R6 semi-detached pair?
faq.a: Whatever the registered party-wall agreement / easement on the two titles says — the 0.0 m side yard at the common line is a zoning permission, not a maintenance agreement.
